_note: Candidate digests for hunt-anon-read and hunt-authz-session. Full hunter text for hunt-anon-write and hunt-sinks-supply lives in the tool-output files named in the critic prompt. Digests are the parent parent's transcription of the hunters' own JSON; titles and traces are verbatim, impacts are compressed.

hunt-anon-read.title: Anonymous read surface is platform-wide, not tenant-scoped: any visitor can dump every tenant's business profile, weekly hours, closed-day exceptions and price catalogue by dropping the client-side .eq('business_id', ...) filter
hunt-anon-read.attack_class: Missing tenant or owner enforcement / Policy and query disagreement / Enumeration and aggregate oracles
hunt-anon-read.trace: attacker calls PostgREST directly with the bundled anon key, e.g. GET /rest/v1/schedules?select=* -> src/config/supabase.ts:14 presents the anon role -> policy body at 0001:97/98/99/100 contains no business_id or slug predicate -> rows for every business returned; tenant restriction exists only in client code at agendaAdapter.ts:93-95
hunt-anon-read.impact: Whole-platform disclosure to an unauthenticated caller: every tenant's business name/slug/timezone/whatsapp/branding, weekly working hours, availability exceptions (exact closed dates), and active services with price and currency. The public page needs exactly one slug's rows.
hunt-anon-read.blocker: Confirm the anon role actually holds SELECT on the four base tables; neither migration issues those grants. Check: SELECT has_table_privilege('anon','public.schedules','SELECT').

hunt-anon-read.title: businesses.owner_id (auth.users UUID of the business owner) is returned to anonymous visitors but is never used by the public flow
hunt-anon-read.boundary: supabase/migrations/0001_agenda_schema.sql:97 anon_read_business using (true) over owner_id declared at 0001:10
hunt-anon-read.trace: select('*') (attacker-replaceable with select=owner_id) -> 0001:10 owner_id uuid references auth.users(id) -> 0001:97 grants the whole row to anon -> response contains the owner's auth.users primary key for every business; required-by-page check: PublicBookingPage.tsx:134 uses only business.name, AgendaContext.tsx:173 only business.id, types.ts:3-10 declares no consumer
hunt-anon-read.impact: Disclosure of internal auth-user identifiers for every tenant, enabling stable cross-tenant correlation of owners and reuse as a join key. No privilege escalation inside this folder; the only writer of owner_id is getOrCreateBusiness at agendaAdapter.ts:61-66 using the session's own id. Same grant caveat covers the unused whatsapp_number (0001:12) and branding (0001:13).
hunt-anon-read.blocker: Same anon SELECT grant assumption as AR1.

hunt-anon-read.title: No publication/lifecycle predicate on businesses: an owner cannot take a business off the public booking page except by deleting the row, which cascades away its bookings and reminders
hunt-anon-read.attack_class: Stale authorization and derived copy use
hunt-anon-read.trace: The control that should exist at 0001:97 is a predicate over a publication flag. The table at 0001:6-15 declares id/name/slug/owner_id/timezone/whatsapp_number/branding/created_at and no is_active/is_published/archived_at, and neither migration adds one, so the predicate cannot be written. The owner's only lever is 0001:91 for all, whose DELETE cascades to bookings (0001:53) and reminders (0001:71).
hunt-anon-read.impact: Business data stays world-readable indefinitely after the owner stops using the product or wants to pause bookings; unpublishing requires destroying the tenant's booking history. Availability impact is low because the windows are already public by design, but the gap is real and unfixable without a migration.

hunt-anon-read.title: anon_insert_booking never binds business_id to event_types.business_id, so an anonymous caller can write bookings into an arbitrary other tenant's calendar, where the EXCLUDE constraint then blocks that tenant's real slots
hunt-anon-read.attack_class: Missing tenant or owner enforcement (write side)
hunt-anon-read.trace: attacker-controlled business_id (any UUID) + event_type_id (any active free event type from ANY tenant) -> read both from the platform-wide anon read at 0001:97/98 -> POST /rest/v1/bookings with start_at/end_at of the attacker's choice, cancel_token omitted so the 0001:63 default applies -> 0002:13-18 validates only e.id = event_type_id and e.is_active and coalesce(e.price,0)=0; there is no e.business_id = bookings.business_id and no businesses lookup at all -> row accepted -> lands in the victim's read path at agendaAdapter.ts:78 and the EXCLUDE at 0001:66 blocks the victim's genuine bookings
hunt-anon-read.impact: Cross-tenant integrity and availability damage from one unauthenticated POST: the victim owner sees a confirmed appointment with attacker-chosen customer_name/email/phone for a service they do not offer, the row occupies a real slot, and the primitive repeats to consume the victim's whole bookable day. No in-app remediation: AdminPanelPage.tsx:994-999 offers only 'Cerrar' and the sole mutation path requires a cancel_token.
hunt-anon-read.blocker: Anon must hold INSERT on public.bookings and SELECT on event_types/businesses. The policies are fully source-visible in 0002:8-19; only the privilege grant is a project-level fact.

hunt-anon-read.title: booked_slots is a definer view, so it bypasses the bookings RLS that denies anon; an anonymous caller can read every tenant's occupied-slot map by omitting the client-side business_id filter
hunt-anon-read.attack_class: Missing tenant or owner enforcement / Policy and query disagreement / Enumeration and aggregate oracles
hunt-anon-read.boundary: supabase/migrations/0001_agenda_schema.sql:115-118 view created without security_invoker, granted to anon at :158
hunt-anon-read.trace: attacker calls GET /rest/v1/booked_slots?select=* with the bundled anon key -> 0001:115 create or replace view has no with (security_invoker = true), so the scan of public.bookings runs as the view owner and the table's RLS (anon_read_own_booking using(false) at :108, owner_bookings at :95) is skipped -> :158 already granted SELECT to anon -> rows for every business returned; tenant scoping lives only in client code at agendaAdapter.ts:95
hunt-anon-read.impact: Cross-tenant disclosure of every confirmed and pending booking's exact time window and which service was booked, for all businesses at once, plus a free counting oracle per tenant via Prefer: count=exact. The projection is limited to business_id/event_type_id/start_at/end_at, so no customer identity is exposed, which caps severity at operational-metadata disclosure.

hunt-anon-read.title: public.bookings is attached to the supabase_realtime publication, so if the project's Realtime Authorization setting is disabled, any anonymous WebSocket subscriber receives live customer PII inserts for all tenants
hunt-anon-read.attack_class: Analytics, logs, traces, and diagnostics as alternate readers
hunt-anon-read.boundary: supabase/migrations/0001_agenda_schema.sql:112 alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.bookings;
hunt-anon-read.trace: attacker subscribes to postgres_changes on public/bookings over the public Realtime endpoint using only the anon publishable key from supabase.ts:14 -> 0001:112 has added the table to the supabase_realtime publication -> INSERT payloads carry the full new row, i.e. customer_name/customer_email/customer_phone at 0001:55-57 -> the only filter would be the SELECT policy at :108 (using(false)), which Realtime applies only when the project's Realtime Authorization feature is enabled. The application never subscribes; this is a direct WebSocket subscription by the attacker.
hunt-anon-read.impact: If the toggle is off: real-time, cross-tenant, unauthenticated disclosure of booking PII for the entire platform, strictly worse than the booked_slots view in the same migration. If the toggle is on, anon receives nothing.
hunt-anon-read.blocker: Requires the live project setting Realtime -> Data > Realtime Authorization, which is not in this repository (config.toml contains only project_id).

hunt-anon-read.title: No server-side re-derivation or validation of the booking interval: duration, chosen start time, buffer and schedule window are trusted from the browser, so one anonymous insert with a long end_at consumes an entire day of a tenant's bookable calendar
hunt-anon-read.attack_class: Business logic / Database and downstream query amplification
hunt-anon-read.boundary: supabase/migrations/0001_agenda_schema.sql:64-66 generated slot_range + EXCLUDE, and 0002_booking_free_only.sql:9-19 the only anon write policy
hunt-anon-read.trace: attacker-controlled start_at and end_at (duration_minutes is never sent, only used to derive end_at in the browser at AgendaContext.tsx:162) -> attacker POSTs /rest/v1/bookings directly with a 12-hour range -> 0002:9-19 with check validates only status/payment_status/payment_intent_id and that the event type is active and free; there is no condition on start_at, end_at, end_at - start_at, business timezone, or the tenant's schedules/availability_exceptions rows -> 0001:64 materialises slot_range from the attacker's own interval and :66 EXCLUDE then rejects every legitimate anon booking that overlaps it -> AgendaContext.tsx:200-201 turns that into 'este horario acaba de ser reservado'. The identical absence exists in the second write sink: 0001:145 lets a token holder set end_at = p_new_start + p_duration_minutes with no bound at all.
hunt-anon-read.impact: Cross-tenant availability and integrity loss from a single unauthenticated request: schedules and availability_exceptions are advisory-only, so bookings are accepted outside declared hours, on disabled weekdays, on owner-declared closed dates and in the past; a single wide interval blocks every overlapping slot in that business's day and the primitive repeats to close whole days with no cap; buffer_minutes is never applied; end_at = start_at yields an empty range that EXCLUDE never conflicts on, so unlimited zero-length bookings can be stacked at one instant, defeating the advertised 'Cero Solpes' guarantee; recovery is not available in-product because AdminPanelPage.tsx:994-999 has no delete/cancel.

hunt-anon-read.title: Unbounded anonymous booking inserts: no per-customer, per-day, or per-business cap anywhere in source, so one anonymous client can fill a tenant's calendar arbitrarily far into the future and blow up the owner's unbounded booking load
hunt-anon-read.attack_class: Unbounded buffering and cardinality / Database and downstream query amplification
hunt-anon-read.boundary: supabase/migrations/0002_booking_free_only.sql:9-19 - the with check has no COUNT/existence guard
hunt-anon-read.trace: attacker loop of POSTs with distinct non-overlapping start_at values -> agendaAdapter.ts:172 -> 0002:9-19 accepts each row (all conditions are per-row, none is aggregate) -> 0001:66 accepts each because the intervals do not overlap -> the victim owner's every panel load runs agendaAdapter.ts:78 select('*').eq('business_id', businessId).order('start_at'), which has no date range, no pagination and no limit, so it materialises the entire flooded history in the browser (AgendaContext.tsx:125, rendered at AdminPanelPage.tsx:674/:765) and will saturate at the platform's default max-rows
hunt-anon-read.impact: Per-tenant persistent denial of bookable inventory plus a slow, eventually unusable owner panel, and unbounded growth of the shared bookings table. Recovery requires manual deletion since the product has no deletion path. Blast radius is confined to the targeted tenant because the owner query is filtered by business_id.
hunt-anon-read.blocker: Confirm in the Supabase dashboard whether project-level or per-role request rate limits are enabled for the Data API, and whether any CDN/WAF sits in front of the Vite build. No such control exists in this repository.

hunt-anon-read.title: secure_manage_booking applies the same unvalidated interval and returns the entire bookings row to an anonymous caller holding a URL token
hunt-anon-read.attack_class: Policy and query disagreement / Missing tenant or owner enforcement
hunt-anon-read.trace: attacker-controlled p_new_start and p_duration_minutes -> AgendaContext.tsx:228-233 -> agendaAdapter.ts:190 rpc -> 0001:139-141 requires only that both be non-null, with no bound, no schedule check, no past-time check and no check that the service is still active or free -> :143-147 updates start_at/end_at/status, with the EXCLUDE at :66 as the only overlap control -> :153 return v_booking where the declared return type is the full public.bookings composite (:122), so the response body carries customer_name, customer_email, customer_phone and payment_intent_id. This is also the only reader that works at all: agendaAdapter.ts:183 asks the table directly, which :108 makes return zero rows for anon, so ManageBookingPage.tsx:41 always renders 'Cita Cancelada'.
hunt-anon-read.impact: A token holder can seize any slot for an arbitrarily long interval and can silently re-confirm a pending_payment row to confirmed (:146). The whole bookings row including contact PII and payment_intent_id is returned to an anonymous principal, and it is the only path through which that PII is readable at all, so the effective read surface is wider than the table policy at :108 advertises. Limited because the token is a genuine customer capability over that customer's own row.

hunt-authz-session.title: Attacker-chosen signup slug permanently squats a tenant's public booking URL and locks the legitimate owner out with no error surfaced
hunt-authz-session.boundary: supabase/migrations/0001_agenda_schema.sql#owner_business insert with check owner_id eq auth uid
hunt-authz-session.trace: attacker-chosen email local part (AdminPanelPage.tsx:213 -> :38 signUp -> agendaAdapter.ts:41) -> AgendaContext.tsx:106-110 effect -> :115 getOrCreateBusiness -> agendaAdapter.ts:63 slug = email.split('@')[0] -> :64-68 INSERT public.businesses(slug, owner_id) -> 0001:9 slug text unique not null; the squat row is then served to the public at agendaAdapter.ts:89 under 0001:97
hunt-authz-session.impact: The attacker's tenant permanently occupies the public namespace /hub/agenda/<slug> and the intended business can never obtain it: the unique constraint rejects the legitimate insert, getOrCreateBusiness discards the error and returns null (agendaAdapter.ts:64-69 destructures only data), so loadBusinessData bails at AgendaContext.tsx:116-119 and the owner's panel stays permanently empty with nothing shown. The same collision self-DoSes any legitimate owner whose address local part matches an earlier registrant. 0001:91 is for all, so any registered owner can also re-point their own slug with a direct PATCH, and there is no rename or reclaim UI anywhere.

hunt-authz-session.title: Open signup plus auto-provisioning is an unthrottled tenant/account factory with no captcha, rate limit or ownership gate in source
hunt-authz-session.boundary: supabase/migrations/0001_agenda_schema.sql#owner_business insert with check owner_id eq auth uid
hunt-authz-session.trace: no control exists at AdminPanelPage.tsx:37-45 (password register) or :61-72 / :184-201 (Google OAuth) -> agendaAdapter.ts:41 and :44-50 -> on any resulting session AgendaContext.tsx:115 -> agendaAdapter.ts:64-68 one INSERT into public.businesses per account, plus one auth.users row per account
hunt-authz-session.impact: Unbounded creation of auth users and tenant rows at zero cost, which is the mechanism that mass-produces the slug squat above and a row-growth lever against a store the product documents as one private database per customer (PRODUCT.md:22). A Gmail address is sufficient because any OAuth sign-in auto-provisions a tenant.
hunt-authz-session.blocker: The effective ceiling is Supabase dashboard configuration, not source: whether Confirm email is on, the built-in signup rate limits, and whether hCaptcha/Turnstile is enabled. config.toml is a stub with no auth section.

hunt-authz-session.title: One unconfirmed click permanently destroys a service and cascades away every booking and all customer PII for it
hunt-authz-session.trace: single click on the trash button at AdminPanelPage.tsx:826-832 (onClick={() => deleteEventType(ev.id)}, no window.confirm, no disabled state, no in-flight guard) -> AgendaContext.tsx:268-272 -> agendaAdapter.ts:198-200 delete().eq('id', id) -> 0001:92 authorises the DELETE for the owning tenant -> 0001:54 event_type_id uuid references public.event_types(id) on delete cascade deletes every bookings row for that event type, taking customer_name/customer_email/customer_phone/start_at/cancel_token with it. 0001:17-31 defines no soft-delete, archive or deleted_at column and the folder contains no restore path.
hunt-authz-session.impact: Irreversible loss of the tenant's booking history and of customer PII, with no confirmation, no undo and no tombstone; the tenant's public page silently loses the service. Because the action needs only one interaction, it is also the ideal framed-click target, making the missing frame protection consequential rather than cosmetic. The rest of the app does use window.confirm for a comparable destructive action at ManageBookingPage.tsx:23, so the omission is a deliberate-looking gap rather than a project-wide convention.
hunt-authz-session.blocker: Framing only. The data-destruction half is source-confirmed. The frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options/CSP response headers are set by the out-of-target host or CDN; index.html is not the served document. Check: curl -I the live /hub/agenda/panel.

hunt-authz-session.title: Privileged service writes report success unconditionally, so a rejected create or update is invisible to the owner
hunt-authz-session.trace: duplicate service title -> AdminPanelPage.tsx:327 slug derivation and :328-338 onSave -> AdminPanelPage.tsx:946-949 onSave={async data => { await saveEventType(data); notify(data.id ? 'Servicio actualizado' : 'Servicio creado exitosamente', 'success') }} which never inspects the returned { data, error } -> AgendaContext.tsx:238-240 returns the Supabase error -> agendaAdapter.ts:195 insert -> 0001:30 unique(business_id, slug) rejects the second service with the same derived slug with 23505
hunt-authz-session.impact: The owner is shown 'Servicio creado exitosamente' for a write that never committed, so the published service list silently diverges from what the owner believes is bookable, and the false success also masks RLS denials. The same unconditional toast is the only feedback any privileged write in this panel produces: deleteEventType, upsertSchedule and upsertException all swallow their errors the same way at AgendaContext.tsx:269-271, :250, :264.

hunt-authz-session.title: Availability toggle and time inputs can commit duplicate schedule rows for the same weekday because the schema has no uniqueness and the client resolves the existing row from a stale closure
hunt-authz-session.trace: owner clicks the availability toggle twice before React re-renders -> AdminPanelPage.tsx:904-911 onClick={handleToggle} (no disabled/pending state) and :919/:925 onChange with no debounce -> AdminPanelPage.tsx:886-889 saveSchedule(dow, '09:00', '18:00') -> AgendaContext.tsx:243-259 resolves the existing row from the render-time closure at :245 schedules.find(s => s.day_of_week === dayOfWeek), finds none, takes the INSERT branch at :256 -> agendaAdapter.ts:204 insert -> 0001:33-40 declares schedules with no unique(business_id, day_of_week), so both rows commit. Slot generation then resolves the day with schedules.find(...) at AgendaContext.tsx:147, i.e. whichever row the API returned first.
hunt-authz-session.impact: The owner's availability for that weekday is decided by an arbitrary row, so the published slot grid can disagree with the configured hours; saveSchedule(dow, null, null) at AgendaContext.tsx:247-252 deletes only the first match, so toggling the day off leaves the duplicate in place and the day stays bookable after the UI reports it as deactivated. The client-side dedupe assumption at :245 and the schema's lack of a uniqueness constraint disagree.

hunt-authz-session.title: Session fixation: a token pair placed in the URL fragment is adopted as the app's session, silently placing the victim inside an attacker-owned tenant
hunt-authz-session.trace: attacker crafts <app-origin>/hub/agenda/panel#access_token=<attacker JWT>&token_type=bearer&expires_in=3600 (the panel path is published in the app's own UI at HomePage.tsx:108 and :135) -> supabase.ts:14-24 constructs the client with no detectSessionInUrl override and no flowType, so the library default URL-session detection runs on the first auth call -> AgendaContext.tsx:101 agendaAdapter.getSession() -> agendaAdapter.ts:28-31 supabase.auth.getSession() -> the client parses the fragment, calls setSession and persists the result to qaway_agenda_auth_token (supabase.ts:19) -> AgendaContext.tsx:102 onAuthStateChange -> setSession(s) with no issuer, audience, session or state check -> AgendaContext.tsx:106-110 fires loadBusinessData -> the victim operates the panel as the attacker's tenant, so everything entered from AdminPanelPage.tsx:434 onward is written into, and later readable by, the attacker via agendaAdapter.ts:73-86 under their own token
hunt-authz-session.impact: Attacker-controlled session context with no visible cue: the victim sees a normal, populated panel, and everything they subsequently create or change belongs to a tenant the attacker owns and can read and modify with their own token. This is the classic OAuth login-CSRF / session-fixation direction and is the exact capability the namespaced session at rest then persists across browser restarts.
hunt-authz-session.blocker: The resolved library version behind the floating @supabase/supabase-js ^2.110.0 (package.json:14) and its URL-session validation behaviour cannot be confirmed from source; there is no node_modules and execution is prohibited. The source-visible half is certain (no detectSessionInUrl override, no flowType, blind onAuthStateChange at :102); the library half is not.

hunt-authz-session.title: The 'Recordarme' control is decorative: unchecking it does not stop the session and refresh token from being persisted to localStorage
hunt-authz-session.trace: AdminPanelPage.tsx:242-251 renders a 'Recordarme' checkbox bound to rememberMe (declared at :22, written only at :247) which is read by no other line in the entire target -> meanwhile supabase.ts:20 hardcodes persistSession: true, so every sign-in (agendaAdapter.ts:37 password, :44-50 OAuth) writes the access and refresh tokens to localStorage['qaway_agenda_auth_token'] (supabase.ts:19) and AgendaContext.tsx:101 reloads them automatically on the next visit
hunt-authz-session.impact: A control the UI presents as a session-persistence choice has no effect at all: the refresh token remains in localStorage after the tab closes and is re-adopted on the next visit, so the next person at that machine is signed in as the previous owner with full tenant write access.
